fields.title: Expression of interest for implementing partner at SWISSAID Tanzania – October 2026
fields.description: Terms of Reference for Implementing Partner for the Power of Diversity Project 1. Background SWISSAID Tanzania has secured funding from the Crop Trust through the Power of Diversity Funding Facility to implement a project entitled “Strengthening Value Chain Coordination and Consumer Awareness for Bambara Groundnut and Sweet Potato Leaves in Tanzania.” The project will run from October 2026 to March 2029 and seeks to strengthen demand-driven development of two neglected and underutilized species (NUS): Bambara groundnut and sweet potato leaves through market coordination, consumer awareness, agroecological production systems, participatory guarantee systems (PGS), women’s economic empowerment, youth engagement, and market systems innovation. Implementing Partner – TOR The intervention will be implemented primarily in Dodoma and Singida regions and will complement ongoing initiatives including BOLDER (World Vegetable Centre), CROPS4HD and AgroEcoNUS+, creating synergies across production, market development, financial inclusion, and policy engagement. SWISSAID is seeking a qualified Tanzanian organization to serve as an implementation partner. 2. Objective To identify a technically competent and legally compliant Tanzanian organization capable of supporting implementation of project activities related to: Agroecological production systems. Neglected and Underutilized Species (NUS) promotion specifically Bambara groundnuts and sweet potato value chains. Market systems development through the participatory market chain approach (PMCA). Agroecology products consumer awareness and behavior change campaigns. Gender equality and inclusion in agroecology and food systems. Monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting. 3. Scope of work The selected partner shall work closely with SWISSAID Tanzania to plan, coordinate, and implement project interventions in the target regions and communities. The partner will be expected to provide both technical leadership and field-level implementation support, ensuring that project objectives, outputs, and outcomes are achieved in accordance with approved workplans, budgets, donor requirements, and SWISSAID policies and standards. The partner will be responsible for the implementation of agreed project activities, including but not limited to the following:Advertisement A. Community mobilization and producer organization Identify, mobilize, and engage farmers, producer groups, women’s groups, youth groups, traders, processors, and other relevant value chain actors in the target locations. Facilitate the establishment, strengthening, and capacity development of farmer organizations and producer groups involved in Bambara groundnut and sweet potato production and marketing. Build and maintain effective collaboration with Local Government Authorities (LGAs), dealers, extension services, private sector actors, community-based organizations, and other stakeholders relevant to the project. Facilitate multi-stakeholder dialogue and coordination platforms aimed at strengthening collaboration and addressing bottlenecks within the selected value chains. B. Agroecological production support Provide technical support to farmers and producer groups on agroecological approaches that enhance productivity, resilience, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable natural resource management. Promote climate-resilient and environmentally sustainable production practices for Bambara groundnut, sweet potato leaves, and other relevant neglected and underutilized species (NUS) IN Singida, Manyoni, Bahi and Chamwino districts. Support farmer learning processes through demonstration plots like Bihawana in Dodoma, farmer field schools, peer-to-peer learning, exchange visits, and practical field-based extension approaches. Facilitate documentation, promotion, and scaling of indigenous knowledge and local innovation related to production, seed management, processing, and utilization of NUS crops. Support on-farm conservation and community-based management of agricultural biodiversity and associated genetic resources. C. Value chain and market systems development Conduct value chain assessments, stakeholder mapping, and market analyses to identify opportunities and constraints affecting production, processing, marketing, and consumption of the target crops. Facilitate market systems development through participatory market chain approach (PMCA) interventions that improve coordination, efficiency, and competitiveness of the selected value chains from existing initiatives like CROPS4HD, BOLDER, and AgrEcoNUS+. Support producers and producer organizations to improve market readiness, product quality, aggregation, packaging, storage, and business management practices. Identify and facilitate relationships between producers, aggregators, processors, traders, retailers, institutional buyers, and other market actors. Promote inclusive business models that increase participation and benefits for women, youth, and marginalized groups. Support development of commercially viable enterprises and income-generating opportunities within the target value chains. D. Consumer awareness and demand creation In collaboration with the SWISSAID team, design and implement consumer awareness and behavior change initiatives using SuLiA and COM-B approaches to increase knowledge, appreciation, adoption, and consumption of Bambara groundnut, sweet potato leaves, and other nutrient-dense indigenous foods. Develop and implement promotional campaigns targeting consumers, schools, local markets, food vendors, restaurants, institutional buyers, and relevant public audiences. Organize fairs, exhibitions, food festivals, cooking demonstrations, tasting events, media engagements, and other awareness-raising activities that promote the nutritional, economic, and environmental benefits of NUS crops. Support the development and dissemination of communication materials, success stories, and awareness products that contribute to increased demand and market visibility. E. Gender equality and inclusion Ensure meaningful participation (at least 60%) of women and youth in all project activities and decision-making processes. Identify and address barriers limiting women’s and young people’s participation in production, value addition, enterprise development, and market engagement. Facilitate access to business development services, entrepreneurship support, financial literacy, and market opportunities for women and youth-led enterprises. Promote leadership and representation of women, youth, and other less privileged social groups within producer organizations, value chain platforms, and community-level structures. F. Monitoring, learning and reporting Develop and maintain robust systems for activity tracking, performance monitoring, data collection, and reporting. Collect high-quality quantitative and qualitative data based on the project’s monitoring framework and donor requirements. Contribute to baseline studies, outcome monitoring, reviews, evaluations, case studies, and learning exercises. Document lessons learned, innovations, best practices, and evidence of impact for knowledge sharing and project learning. Participate in periodic planning, reflection, review, and learning meetings organized by SWISSAID. Prepare and submit timely technical, financial, and narrative reports as per agreed reporting schedules. Participate in project planning, budgeting, review, coordination, and donor engagement processes as requested by SWISSAID. Maintain accurate project records and supporting documentation for audit and verification purposes. Contribute to the achievement of project outcomes, indicators, and targets through proactive implementation, adaptive management, and continuous improvement. 4. Required qualifications and experience Interested organizations must demonstrate: Institutional capacity Legally registered local non-government and non-profit making organization operating in Tanzania Mainland. Minimum 5 years of proven experience implementing agroecology development programmes. Presence and operational capacity in Dodoma and/or Singida regions is highly desirable. Must not be currently supported by or implementing any SWISSAID project. Technical expertise (mandatory) Applicants must demonstrate substantial technical expertise and a proven track record in designing and implementing agricultural and rural development programmes that contribute to resilient, inclusive, and sustainable food systems. Particular preference will be given to organizations with demonstrated experience in agroecology, neglected and underutilized species (NUS), and market systems approaches that create sustainable livelihood opportunities for smallholder farmers, women, and youth. Programme management Experience managing donor-funded projects. Strong planning, financial management, and reporting systems. Demonstrated MEL capacity. Ability to work with local government authorities and private sector actors. 5. Compliance requirements (mandatory) Applicants must submit: Certificate of Registration. Valid Tax Identification Number (TIN). Tax Clearance Certificate (if applicable). NGO Compliance Certificate (where applicable) or recently submitted annual returns. Most recent audited financial statements (last 2 years). Organizational profile. Anti-fraud, financial, procurement, code of conduct, human resource, safeguarding, and conflict of interest policies. Evidence of statutory compliance with all applicable Tanzanian laws and regulations. At least three references from recent donors or funding partners. Failure to provide any mandatory compliance documentation may lead to disqualification. 6. Expected deliverables The selected partner will be expected to deliver:Advertisement Annual implementation workplans. Quarterly technical reports. Quarterly financial reports. Activity reports and supporting documentation. Beneficiary databases and monitoring data. Success stories and learning products. Contribution to annual reviews and evaluation activities. 7. Application requirements Interested organizations should submit: Expression of Interest (maximum 5 pages). Technical proposal demonstrating understanding of the assignment. Organizational profile. CVs of key personnel. Relevant organizational experience and project references. Statutory compliance documents listed above. Interested organizations should submit their expression of interest through [email protected] before Thursday 8th October 2026, 17:00pm. 8. Equal opportunity SWISSAID is committed to a fair, transparent, and non-discriminatory partner selection process. All applications will be evaluated solely on the basis of technical expertise, organizational capacity, relevant experience, statutory compliance, and the ability to achieve the objectives of the assignment. SWISSAID encourages applications from qualified organizations that demonstrate a commitment to gender equality, youth inclusion, safeguarding, and the promotion of inclusive and sustainable food systems. The selected partner will be expected to uphold the highest standards of integrity, accountability, ethical conduct, and compliance with applicable laws and regulations. Disclaimer SWISSAID reserves the right to accept or reject any application and to cancel or modify the selection process at any stage without incurring any liability to applicants.Advertisement All costs associated with the preparation and submission of applications shall be borne by the applicant. Submission of an application does not constitute a commitment by SWISSAID to provide funding or enter into a partnership agreement. Any engagement will be subject to successful completion of the selection process and the signing of a formal agreement. READ ALSO: All Tenders and JOBS IN TANZANIA Advertisement

fields.title: Programme Coordinator – Extractive Industry Project at SWISSAID – October 2026
fields.description:
Programme Coordinator – Extractive Industry Project

Duty station: Geita, Tanzania
Reports to: Head of Programmes
Geographical coverage: Geita and Shinyanga, with regular travel to Dar es Salaam and other locations as required. Job Vacancy - Programme Coordin…
Background

SWISSAID is implementing a 3 yeas Extractive Industries Phase III project funded by FGC which builds on SWISSAID’s previous work in Tanzania’s extractive sector. Phase I addressed governance across mining, oil and gas, with a focus on transparency and safety in artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM).

Phase II (2023–2025) narrowed the intervention to ASM governance and safety, strengthening accountability demands and piloting practical improvements through model artisanal and small-scale gold mines.

Phase III (2026–2028) consolidates these achievements by focusing on the governance of the artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) sector, which generates up to 40% of Tanzania’s mining revenues. The project is implemented in partnership with Rafiki SDO and HakiRaslimali for technical field implementation, while strengthening community monitoring, transparency, traceability and inclusive governance.

It will also reinforce civil society networks, multi-stakeholder collaboration and targeted support to women miners’ cooperatives in Geita and Shinyanga, ensuring sustainability through local ownership and collaboration with local government authorities.
Purpose of the position

The Programme Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the day-to-day implementation, monitoring and reporting of SWISSAID’s Extractive Industry Project in Geita and Shinyanga, including coordination with partners implementing research, advocacy and policy-related activities based in Dar es Salaam.

Under the supervision of the Head of Programmes, the Coordinator will ensure timely and quality implementation of project activities in accordance with approved plans, budgets, donor requirements and SWISSAID policies.

The position will work closely with partners, communities, government authorities, civil society and other stakeholders to achieve project results.
Key duties and responsibilities

1. Project coordination and monitoring

- Coordinate implementation of project activities in Geita and Shinyanga according to approved work plans, budgets and timelines.

- Monitor project progress, results and indicators and identify implementation challenges requiring management attention.

- Conduct regular field monitoring visits and provide technical and implementation support to partners.

- Coordinate project planning, review and learning meetings.

- Document results, lessons learned, good practices and stories of change.

- Contribute to project evaluations, assessments and programme learning.

2. Partner coordination and capacity strengthening

- Maintain effective collaboration and regular communication with implementing partners Rafiki SDO and HakiRaslimali.

- Support partners in project planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting.

- Monitor implementation of partner agreements and follow up on agreed deliverables.

- Identify capacity gaps and support capacity strengthening of project partners.

- Ensure partners understand and comply with SWISSAID policies, procedures and relevant donor requirements.

3. Research, advocacy and stakeholder engagement

- Coordinate and support project-related research, advocacy and policy activities implemented by partners.

- Contribute field evidence, data and case studies for research, advocacy and policy engagement.

- Contribute to policy briefs, research products, presentations and other relevant publications.

- Build constructive relationships with local government, mining stakeholders, communities, CSOs and other relevant actors.

- Represent SWISSAID in project-related meetings and forums when delegated by the Head of Programmes and approved by Country Representative.

4. Financial monitoring and compliance

- Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and work plans.

- Review partner fund requests and financial reports for completeness and consistency before submission for further review and approval.

- Work closely with Finance/Administration to ensure appropriate financial documentation and accountability.

- Support partners to understand and comply with financial procedures and donor requirements.

- Report significant budget deviations, financial irregularities or compliance concerns promptly to the Head of Programmes.

- Support project audits and follow-up of audit recommendations where applicable.

5. Reporting and programme development

- Prepare timely and quality monthly, quarterly, annual and donor project reports as required.

- Maintain proper project records and documentation.

- Provide regular implementation updates to the Head of Programmes.

- Contribute technical and field information to new project concepts, proposals and fundraising initiatives.

- Provide programme information, evidence and success stories for communication and donor engagement.

6. Gender, youth and cross-cutting issues

- Mainstream gender equality, youth participation, social inclusion, environmental sustainability and climate change considerations throughout project implementation.

- Promote meaningful participation of women, youth and affected communities.

- Ensure safeguarding, accountability and participation principles are respected during implementation.

7. Teamwork

- Work closely with the Head of Programmes, Country Representative, Finance/Administration and other SWISSAID Tanzania staff.

- Foster teamwork, constructive collaboration and a results-oriented working culture.

- Participate actively in programme planning, review and learning processes.

Qualifications and experience

- Bachelor’s degree in development studies, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Studies, Mining Engineering, Geographical Information Systems, Economics, Mining-related studies or another relevant field.

- Minimum 4 years of relevant professional experience in development project/programme coordination and implementation.

- Experience in extractive industries, artisanal and small-scale mining, natural resource governance, governance/accountability or community development is highly desirable.

- Experience coordinating partners, monitoring projects and preparing quality reports.

- Experience in budget monitoring and donor-funded projects is desirable.

- Strong stakeholder engagement, analytical, organisational and communication skills.

- Good written and spoken English and Kiswahili.

- Ability to work independently and travel regularly within project areas.

Other duties

This job description outlines the main duties of the position and is not exhaustive. The post holder may undertake other reasonable responsibilities related to the role as assigned by the Head of Programmes.
Positioning

This JD appropriately places the role at Programme Coordinator/mid-level, consistent with a 53,187,714 TZS per annum gross monthly salary, while keeping strategic programme leadership, final financial accountability, HR authority and senior representation with the Head of Programmes and Country Representative.

How to Apply:
Please send your CV and Cover Letter to info@swissaidtanzania.org before Thursday 8th October 2026, 17:00pm.

To supervise and coordinate pollination and emasculation activities within the assigned production area, ensuring that activities are carried out efficiently, accurately, and in accordance with required quality and production standards.

The role will also provide day-to-day supervision of assigned teams, support crop management activities, identify and communicate operational or crop-related concerns, and ensure adherence to company, quality, hygiene, health and safety, and farm protocols.

- Good communication and interpersonal skills, with proficiency in English and Swahili languages and the ability to work effectively with employees and different teams.

- Basic computer skills and the ability to maintain and communicate relevant operational information and records.

We offer a competitive salary, benefit package and an innovative environment. Teamwork, entrepreneurship, drive, a passion to learn and to share knowledge, respect for sustainable development and integrity are our most precious values.

Our international work environment offers a range of possibilities to motivated qualified people with excellent interpersonal and organizational skills.

fields.title: Psychosocial & Health Coordinator job at The Foundation For Tomorrow (TFFT) October 2026
fields.description:
Psychosocial & Health Coordinator

The Foundation For Tomorrow (TFFT) | Arusha, Tanzania
Empowering Through Education

- Location: Arusha, Tanzania

- Reports to: Scholarship Program Manager

- Technical collaboration: Scholarship Program Operations and Development Coordinator

- Application deadline: 25th October 2026 Psychosocial and Health Coordin…

About TFFT

TFFT is an international nonprofit working to secure quality education and emotional support for orphaned and vulnerable children in Tanzania, so they can reach their full potential and thrive in their communities. Our Scholarship Program walks with scholars from enrolment through graduation, our Teacher Training Program strengthens instruction in partner schools, and our Community Learning Centre in Usa River extends that work into the wider community.
The role

The Psychosocial & Health Coordinator leads the wellbeing side of the Scholarship Program — psychosocial support, case management, safeguarding, family engagement, and health coordination — so that every scholar is safe, healthy, and able to thrive academically, socially, and personally. The role works closely with scholars, caregivers, schools, health providers, government authorities, and community stakeholders throughout the scholarship journey.
What you will do

- Scholar wellbeing and psychosocial support: Monitor scholars' social, emotional, and psychological wellbeing through regular assessments, provide direct psychosocial support within professional limits, and design individualized wellbeing plans, referring to specialist services where needed.

- Case management: Lead scholar case management from intake through confidential documentation, multidisciplinary case reviews, and resolution, including tailored pathway and mentorship planning built around each scholar's strengths.

- Child protection and safeguarding: Implement TFFT's Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: identify and respond to concerns, coordinate investigations with government authorities where required, and build safeguarding awareness among scholars, staff, caregivers, and partner schools.

- Family and community engagement: Conduct home visits, build strong relationships with caregivers and community stakeholders, and run family meetings and caregiver forums that strengthen the support around each scholar.

- Health and welfare coordination: Coordinate health assessments, referrals, and emergency support, and maintain accurate health records in collaboration with local providers.

- School-based support: Partner with school leaders, teachers, and counsellors to address wellbeing, behavioural, and attendance concerns, and strengthen school capacity on safeguarding and psychosocial support.

- Scholar engagement: Support engagement and enrichment activities, and bring a wellbeing lens to recruitment, selection, onboarding, and school transitions across the Scholarship Program.

- Training and capacity building: Design and deliver training on safeguarding, child protection, and psychosocial support for TFFT staff, caregivers, and school personnel, and develop supporting resource materials.

- Data, monitoring, and reporting: Maintain wellbeing and case management data, track key indicators, prepare regular reports for TFFT Tanzania and TFFT US, and help document scholar impact stories.

- Collaboration: Work across TFFT's teams, represent TFFT in stakeholder engagements, and support organizational priorities such as continuous improvement, fundraising, and donor reporting as needed.

Who we're looking for

Education: Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counselling, Sociology, Community Development, Guidance and Counselling, or a related field.

Preferred: Professional certification in counselling, child protection, safeguarding, or case management.

Experience: At least 3 years' experience in child protection, case management, psychosocial support, social work, or youth development programs.
Key competencies

- Child safeguarding, protection, and case management

- Psychosocial support, counselling, active listening, and mental health promotion

- Family and community engagement

- Health referral and coordination

- Training and facilitation

- Project Design, Strategic Planning, and Management

- Monitoring, evaluation, reporting, and confidential data management

- Stakeholder relationship management and excellent interpersonal skills

- Conflict resolution and problem-solving

- Planning, coordination, and organizational skills

- Report writing and documentation

- Teamwork and collaboration

- Empathy, cultural sensitivity, and a high level of integrity and professionalism

Our commitment to safeguarding

TFFT is committed to safeguarding the children in our programs, and every member of our team shares that responsibility. Offers of employment are subject to reference checks and background clearance.
How to apply

Send a CV and cover letter to jobs@thefoundationfortomorrow.org with the subject line "Psychosocial & Health Coordinator Application."
Deadline of application: 25th October 2026.

NOTE: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

fields.title: Graduate Career Launchpad (6‑Week Programme)
fields.description:
The Graduate Career Launchpad is a six‑week intensive programme offered by Kryptr, a technology and human capital development firm operating within the Education & EdTech sector. This experience is designed for recent graduates who aim to secure their first full‑time role by 2027. Participants will collaborate with mentors, industry experts and real‑world companies to acquire practical workplace abilities. You will report to a dedicated programme coordinator who will guide you through each module and ensure you meet the learning objectives.
Why Join KRYPTR
Kryptr focuses on bridging the gap between education and employment, giving you access to tools and networks that many new graduates lack. By joining the Launchpad, you become part of a community that values continuous learning and real‑world impact. The programme blends theoretical instruction with hands‑on projects, allowing you to build a portfolio that demonstrates your readiness to employers. You will also benefit from personalised mentorship from professionals who understand the challenges of entering the job market.
What You'll Do
During the six weeks you will immerse yourself in a structured curriculum that balances skill development with practical application.
- Complete interactive modules that cover essential workplace competencies such as communication, time management and problem‑solving.
- Explore introductory concepts in Business Analysis, Human Resources and Customer Success or Sales through guided case studies.
- Collaborate with small teams to develop solutions for real business briefs supplied by partner organisations.
- Present your findings and recommendations to mentors and receive constructive feedback to refine your approach.
- Document your contributions in a professional portfolio that showcases the skills and results you have achieved.
- Participate in weekly mentorship sessions where industry experts share insights on career pathways and interview preparation.
- Engage in peer‑review activities that strengthen your ability to give and receive constructive criticism.
- Reflect on personal development goals and track progress against the programme’s competency framework.

What We're Looking For
Successful candidates will demonstrate a genuine commitment to launching a professional career and possess the foundational attributes needed for rapid learning.
- A recent graduate or final‑year university student from any discipline.
- Strong interest in at least one of the focus areas: Business Analysis, Human Resources or Customer Success/Sales.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate ideas clearly.
- Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a team setting and respect diverse viewpoints.
- Basic proficiency with digital collaboration tools such as document editors, video‑conferencing platforms and project‑management software.
- Self‑motivation to complete assignments on schedule and seek feedback proactively.
- Availability to commit to the full six‑week schedule, including live workshops and mentor meetings.

Perks & Benefits
Participants receive mentorship from seasoned professionals, a certificate of completion, and a curated portfolio of work that can be shared with prospective employers. The programme also offers networking opportunities with partner companies that frequently consider graduates for entry‑level positions.
If you are ready to invest time in building the capabilities that will set you apart in the 2027 job market, we encourage you to this platform. Your journey towards a successful first job begins with the right preparation, and Kryptr is here to support you every step of the way.
